If you want to focus on shipping features rather than managing database overhead, give SQLite a second chance. It is the underrated hero of modern web development.

n06.C: Think of a CDN as a global network of warehouses for your website's content. Instead of every visitor traveling to your single server across the world to grab data, the CDN delivers files from the server physically closest to them. By caching images, scripts, and pages at the "edge," it drastically reduces lag and prevents server crashes. It is the hidden secret sauce that makes a website feel instantaneous, regardless of whether your reader is browsing from Tokyo, New York, or London.
n06.A:
Ever wonder why some websites feel instantaneous while others crawl? The secret is a CDN.

Think of a CDN as a global network of local warehouses for your website's content. Instead of every visitor traveling to one central server halfway across the world, the CDN delivers files from a location physically closest to them. By caching images and scripts at the "edge," it slashes latency and prevents server crashes. It is the invisible engine that makes your site feel lightning-fast, whether your reader is in Tokyo, New York, or London.
n06.B:
Think of a Content Delivery Network (CDN) as a global network of local warehouses for the internet. Instead of every user in the world having to request data from one single, central server—which causes lag and delays—the CDN stores copies of your website's files in data centers all over the globe. 

When someone visits your site, the CDN serves the content from the server physically closest to them. This reduces latency, speeds up loading times, and keeps your site stable even during traffic spikes.

n07.C: Password managers are the gold standard for security because they allow us to use unique, complex strings for every site without mental effort. The ultimate safety net is a long, memorized passphrase—something memorable that allows you to recover your accounts if the tech fails. Ultimately, use a manager for daily convenience, but master one phrase for total peace of mind.
n07.A:
Don't choose between a password manager and your memory—use both.

Password managers are the gold standard for security, enabling unique, complex credentials for every site without mental fatigue. But a digital vault is only as secure as its master key; if you lose access, you're locked out of your own life. The ultimate safety net is a single, long, memorized passphrase. Use a manager for daily convenience, but master one unbreakable phrase for total peace of mind.
n07.B:
The debate between password managers and memorized passphrases often feels like a choice between convenience and control. Relying on memory is great for a handful of accounts, but as our digital footprint grows, it becomes impossible to maintain unique, high-entropy strings for every site.

Password managers take the mental load off, allowing you to use massive, randomized strings that are virtually unhackable. While a master passphrase is a vital fallback, a manager is the only way to ensure you aren't reusing the same "strong" password everywhere.

A pipeline is only as strong as the confidence a green light actually provides.

While the savings depend on your brightness settings and UI design, it's still one of the easiest ways to squeeze extra life out of your phone while reducing eye strain during late-night scrolls.

While the exact savings depend on your brightness and UI design, switching to dark mode is one of the easiest ways to squeeze extra life out of your phone and reduce eye strain.

n12.C:

By minute five, you’re checking status pages on your phone, praying the rest of the world isn't with you. By minute ten, the silence of the screen feels heavy, and you realize just how much your daily life depends on fragile, invisible servers.
n12.A:

By minute five, you’re scrolling status pages on your phone, praying the rest of the world isn't joining you. By minute ten, the silence of a dead screen feels heavy. You realize, with a sudden sinking feeling, just how much your daily life depends on a web of fragile, invisible servers.
